messages:
lina: Quick question — ZetaCorp wants to run 3 parallel POCs and asked if we can stack commits/discounts across them instead of treating each as separate POC. They want credits applied to each POC and then a single consolidated commit if they go to prod. Thoughts?
marco: Stacking is possible but depends on billing entity and contract boundaries. We normally aggregate at org-level (billing account). If they have 3 subsidiaries with separate legal entities, we can't automatically combine.
kate: Deal Desk: we can do a consolidated commit offer, but need explicit mapping in the SOW. Proposal: 1) define BILLING_ENTITY in SOW, 2) specify POC tags, 3) cap stacking to X total commit units.
sam: Also important: the POCs use different models + instance types, so per-token economics will vary. Need to call out model-specific rate multipliers or we'll under/over price.
jess: From RevOps: for billing, we need a clear flag to mark usage as POC-exempt or POC-credit. If you want no charge during POC window, we mark usage with tag `poc_free=true` and exclude from invoicing. Otherwise apply credits after invoicing.
lina: Customer ask: "no usage charge for POC, credits reserved and applied if they sign within 90 days". Is a 90-day window ok operationally?
kate: We can do a 90d conversion window. Must include: "POC credits expire after 90 days; credits cannot be transferred across billing entities; stacking limited to 2 active POCs per legal entity unless Deal Desk approves exception."
marco: Technical caveat — if they spin up multiple endpoints under same project, KV cache/cost savings may overlap. Should warn customer that combined POC utilization might not linearly sum.
lina: Good call. I'll add a note in the quote: "Shared infra optimizations may change per-POC cost assumptions."
jess: Workflow for ops: If we do POC-exempt billing, ops team needs a CSV with columns: BILLING_ENTITY, POC_TAG, START_TS, END_TS, COMMIT_ID. We can import into billing system.
ops-bot: Reminder — create deal desk ticket using /deal-request and attach SOW + mapping CSV. Template: https://confluence.redwood/poc-commit-matrix (internal).
kate: Example mapping snippet to include in SOW (for Deal Desk and RevOps):
```
BILLING_ENTITY=ZetaCorp-Holdings
POC_TAG=ZETA-POC-2026-03
POC_WINDOW=2026-04-01 to 2026-06-30
POC_CREDIT=100% of usage for POC window, up to $30,000 per POC
CONSOLIDATED_COMMIT=Apply up to $60,000/mo for 12 months if signed within 90d
CREDIT_EXPIRATION=90d
STACKING_LIMIT=2 active POCs per billing entity without Deal Desk approval
```
kate: That snippet is provisional. Legal will need to sign off on the language for credits/refunds.
legal-bot: Legal note — no refunds for committed fees. Credits can be applied to future invoices but should be capped and timeboxed. Include audit clause for POC usages.
marco: One more ops detail: if customer requests "no metering" during POC (completely invisible), that's high risk. Better to meter and tag but invoice $0 via credits so we have telemetry.
lina: Agree — we need telemetry for production sizing. I'll push for metered+credited.
kate: Approving on Deal Desk provisional terms; will prepare deal-request and route to Legal for final language. @lina please attach CSV and model usage estimates.
lina: Will attach CSV and sample traffic profiles by EOD. If legal signs, I'll update quote line items as: POC-CREDIT (line), CONSOLIDATED-COMMIT (line), SKU multipliers (per model).
jess: After sign-off, RevOps will create commit record and tag commit_id to invoices. Also note: if they convert and usage < commit, no refunds (per legal), but unused credits do not auto transfer to other deals.
lina: Thanks team — leaving this here until Legal posts final. :thumbsup:
